extracted.intended_audience: researchers and graduate students in geometric analysis working on Ricci flow and Perelman's proof
extracted.subtask_description: Technical justification and parameter choices to construct long-time solutions to the Ricci flow with surgery on compact orientable three-manifolds, proving preservation of pinching, canonical neighborhood properties, and noncollapsing under finitely many δ-cutoff surgeries. Focuses on lemmas/propositions (Perelman, Hamilton) that give quantitative constraints on δ, r(t), κ, and related parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery removal rules (capped horns, double horns, compact components)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the surgery procedure: (3) throw away all capped horns and double horns lying in Ω; (4) declare extinct all compact components lying in Ωρ. (In Sections 7.6 and 7.7 one may also declare extinct every compact component which has nonnegative scalar curvature.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit topological/procedural steps used to modify the manifold at surgery times; they determine which regions are excised (and hence which points cease to exist thereafter). The text explains these removals are part of the definition of the surgically modified manifold and are used when arguing persistence of assumptions (pinching, canonical neighborhoods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption preserved under surgery
rubrics_metrics.description: After performing δ-cutoff surgeries (at time T), the pinching assumption (7.3.3) still holds for the surgically modified manifold; the surgically modified manifold then serves as initial data for continuing the Ricci flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a requirement on the surgery construction and parameter choices so that the curvature pinching inequalities remain valid across surgery events; the preservation is invoked repeatedly to continue the flow and to apply canonical neighborhood and gradient estimates after surgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: The solution must satisfy the canonical neighborhood assumption with accuracy ε on specified time intervals: every high-curvature point has a neighborhood which is either an ε-neck, an ε-cap, or (excluded) component of positive sectional curvature as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a central structural hypothesis; includes associated gradient estimates (7.3.4). The goal is to find a single nonincreasing positive function r(t) (independent of the stage k of the inductive extension) so the canonical neighborhood assumption (accuracy ε) holds uniformly with r=r(t). The assumption is quantified by constants such as η and C1(ε) and is tied to scale r and curvature thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: δ-cutoff surgery smallness condition (Lemma 7.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any 0 < ε ≤ 1/100, 1 < A < ∞ and 0 < θ < 1 there exists ¯δ = ¯δ(A, θ, ε) with the property: if the Ricci flow with surgery satisfies the a priori assumptions and all δ-cutoff surgeries have δ < ¯δ, then for any gluing cap center x0 and cutoff radius h one of two alternatives holds: (i) the solution is defined on a parabolic neighborhood P(x0,T0,Ah,T1−T0) and, after scaling by h^−2 and shifting time, is A^−1/2-close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution; or (ii) the same holds up to a surgery time t+ and the whole ball B_{T0}(x0,Ah) is cut off at t+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a quantitative criterion (choice of ¯δ depending on A,θ,ε) ensuring local geometric closeness (in scaled C^∞loc sense) to the standard cap/cylinder solution near surgery regions. It includes parabolic region definitions and the dichotomy about whether the region persists or is removed at the next surgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local closeness to the standard solution (quantitative, Corollary/Lemma statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: On specified parabolic regions around gluing caps (after scaling by h^{-2} and shifting time), the solution is, for sufficiently small δ, arbitrarily close (e.g., δ′-close in C^{[δ′^{-1}]} topology) to the corresponding subset of the standard capped infinite cylinder (standard solution) on stated time intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to replace local pieces by the model (standard) solution for estimates (curvature, diameter, neck/cap structure). The statements quantify how choices of A, δ′, and scaling h control the closeness; these are prerequisites for invoking uniqueness/convergence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Perelman distance action lower bound in gluing-cap regions (Corollary 7.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any l < ∞ one can find A = A(l) < ∞ and θ = θ(l) ∈ (0,1) so that for δ < ¯δ(A,θ,ε), any smooth curve γ contained in B_{T0}(x0,Ah) with γ(T0) on the boundary and parametrized until Tγ ≤ min(T1,T0+θ h^2) satisfies ∫_{T0}^{Tγ} (R(γ(t),t) + |γ˙(t)|^2) dt > l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a lower bound on the Perelman L-length (action) of curves penetrating the gluing-cap region, used to estimate reduced distance and to show barely admissible curves contribute large L (hence cannot realize minimizers), which is crucial in reduced-volume/local noncollapsing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of κ-noncollapsed on scales less than ρ
rubrics_metrics.description: A surgically modified solution g_{ij}(t) is κ-noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scales less than ρ if whenever r < ρ and |Rm(x,t)| ≤ r^{-2} holds on P(x0,t0,r,−r^2) (for those (x,t) for which the solution is defined), then Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scale-dependent noncollapsing condition used throughout; it is the target quantitative lower volume bound tied to curvature control on parabolic neighborhoods. It underpins compactness arguments and reduced-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform κ-noncollapsing under small δ surgeries (Lemma 7.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given sequences constructed for previous steps and sufficiently small universal ε, one can find κ > 0 and, for any 0 < r < ε, a δ = δ(r,ε) > 0 so that if a surgically modified solution (with normalized initial data and finitely many surgeries) satisfies the proposition hypotheses on earlier time intervals and the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε) with r on [mε^2,  ar T], and all δ-cutoff surgeries in [(m-1)ε^2, ar T] use δ(t) ≤ min(δ,¯δ(t)), then the solution is κ-noncollapsed on [0, ar T] for all scales less than ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the mechanism to propagate noncollapsing across surgery times given sufficiently small δ choices, relying on localization of Perelman's reduced-volume argument and controlling barely admissible curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissible and barely admissible curves and L-length lower bound (Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A curve is admissible if it stays in the space-time region unaﬀected by surgery; barely admissible curves lie on the boundary of admissible set. For any given L, r, rm, ε there exists ¯δ = ¯δ(L,r,rm,ε) so that any barely admissible curve γ from a gluing cap at surgery time T0 to (x0,t0) satisfies ∫_{T0}^{t0} √{t0−t} (R+(γ(t),t)+|γ˙|^2) dt ≥ L (quantified in (7.4.2) and ensuing estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative lower bound prevents barely admissible curves from achieving small reduced distance; used to ensure minimizing L-curves are admissible (hence the reduced-volume monotonicity/localization argument applies despite surgeries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalized initial metric: scalar curvature lower bound
rubrics_metrics.description: For normalized initial manifolds the scalar curvature satisfies R ≥ 1 at initial time t = 0; by maximum principle the surgically modified solution continues to satisfy R ≥ -1/t or appropriate universal lower bounds in space-time (text uses R ≥ -1/t, and says surgeries occur where scalar curvature is very large).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These curvature normalization/lower-bound hypotheses are used to control the behavior of R in estimates (L-length, reduced volume) and to localize surgeries to high-curvature regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of sequences r_j, δ_j, κ_j to justify canonical neighborhood assumption (Proposition 7.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given small ε>0 there exist decreasing sequences 0 < r_j < ε, δ_j < ε^2, and κ_j > 0 (j=1,2,...) and a positive function δ(t) with δ(t) ≤ min(δ_j, ¯δ(t)) on time intervals [(j-1)ε^2, jε^2) such that any surgically modified solution (normalized initial data, finitely many surgeries with δ(t) as above) satisfies on each time interval [(j-1)ε^2, jε^2) the κ_j-noncollapsing condition on all scales < ε and the canonical neighborhood assumption (accuracy ε) with r = r_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the main inductive criterion: by choosing these sequences appropriately and restricting ¯δ(t), one prevents surgery times from accumulating and obtains uniform canonical neighborhood structure across successive time slabs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery geometry: surgeries along middle two-sphere of δ-neck
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgeries are always performed along the middle two-sphere of a δ-neck; when a ball (e.g., B_{T0}(x0,Ak h)) is removed at a surgery time t+ it is because that ball is part of a capped horn and the whole component is declared extinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric constraint on where cuts are made ensures the removed regions have standard neck/cap geometry, which is crucial to compare to the standard solution and to deduce that points in those regions cannot be centers of δ-necks at nearby times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gradient estimates to propagate curvature bounds and closeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The gradient estimates in the canonical neighborhood assumption (7.3.4) are used to obtain uniform curvature bounds on parabolic regions over short time intervals, hence to apply uniqueness/the compactness theorem and show scaled solutions converge to the standard solution in C^∞loc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates give control of time-derivatives and spatial derivatives of curvature; they are used iteratively (defining A_k sequences) to extend the time interval on which local regions look like the standard solution and to rule out formation of unexpected high-curvature neck centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of Perelman's reduced-volume monotonicity to unaﬀected region
rubrics_metrics.description: Because surgeries remove high-curvature regions, one must localize Perelman's reduced-volume monotonicity to cone-like subsets composed of admissible shortest L-geodesics that remain in unaﬀected region; monotonicity and Jacobian comparison then give a lower bound on reduced-volume of such subsets and hence lower volume bounds for balls at later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument requires ensuring the admissible shortest L-geodesics to points in a suitable ball are entirely unaﬀected by surgery (achieved by choosing δ small and using L-length lower bounds for barely admissible curves), and then applying Jacobian comparison (Theorem 3.2.7) and the usual reduction-to-reduced-volume machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter choice to push surgical regions to infinity in rescaled limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking limits of rescaled surgically modified solutions one must choose δ (e.g., δ_{m+1} ≪ δ_m) small enough so that surgical regions are pushed to spatial infinity in the rescaled solutions, allowing extraction of an orientable ancient κ-solution as a limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the explicit tactic used in the compactness/contradiction part of the proof: by making subsequent δ's sufficiently small relative to the rescaling factors, the local geometry near chosen basepoints is unaffected by surgery in the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-accumulation of surgery times via uniform r(t) and control on ¯δ(t)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent surgery times from accumulating one must choose a single nonincreasing positive function r(t) independent of the induction stage k (i.e., uniform r(t) ≤ r_i(t) for all i) and further restrict the positive function ¯δ(t) so that δ_i < ¯δ(t_i) at each surgery time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures the canonical neighborhood assumption can be justified uniformly in time and the inductive extension of the flow continues unless extinction occurs; it is enforced by the construction of the sequences r_j,δ_j,κ_j and choosing ¯δ(t) appropriately.
